model.description: Which model to use: grok | hermes-3-405b | euryale-70b. Only grok accepts image_assets. All three are uncensored.

prompt.description: The user prompt to send to the model.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt that steers the model.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate (default 2048, max 4096).

image_assets.description: Optional reference image(s) to analyze alongside the prompt (vision-capable models only, e.g. grok).

text.description: The text generated by the model.

metadata.description:
Run an uncensored large language model over a text prompt and return the generated text. Useful as a text-generation or prompt-rewriting node — e.g. inside a workflow to compose or expand a prompt before an image/video tool.

**Models:** `grok` (text + up to 4 reference images — computer vision), `hermes-3-405b`, `euryale-70b` (text-only).

Input: a `model`, a `prompt`, an optional `system_prompt`, an optional `max_tokens`, and optional `image_assets` (grok only). `prompt` and `system_prompt` together must not exceed 32000 characters. Output: the generated `text`.

image_asset.description: Asset ID of the image to upscale (upload via POST /assets).

version.description: Upscale engine. `seedvr2_7b` — premium diffusion-restoration upscale for 4K/6K output, controlled by `detail`/`target_resolution` plus `noise_scale`; `seedvr2_3b` — fast diffusion-restoration upscale controlled by `detail`/`target_resolution`. Default `seedvr2_7b`.

target_resolution.description: Output size tier. `seedvr2_3b` accepts `2k`, `4k`, `8k`; `seedvr2_7b` accepts `4k`, `6k`. Default `4k`.

detail.description: How much of the source is preserved before upscaling — `high` keeps the most source detail (smallest pre-processing budget), `low` allows the most restoration. One of `high`, `medium`, `low`. Default `medium`.

noise_scale.description: `seedvr2_7b` only: amount of synthetic detail added during upscaling, 0-1. Default 0.

image_asset.description: Asset ID of the upscaled image.

metadata.description:
Increase the resolution of an existing image while restoring or adding detail. Best for low-resolution sources that need to be cleaned up and improved; gains are limited on an already-sharp 4K image. Input: one image asset. Output: one higher-resolution image.

**Versions:**
- `seedvr2_7b` *(default)* — Premium diffusion-restoration upscaler for 4K/6K output; `detail` and `target_resolution` control it, plus `noise_scale`.
- `seedvr2_3b` — Fast diffusion-restoration upscaler; `detail` and `target_resolution` control it.

ref_asset.description: Asset ID of the target image whose face will be replaced.

face_asset.description: Asset ID of the image providing the new face.

model.description: Face-swap model: `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` (default), a full-head variant or a MuleRouter swap.

tier.description: Output resolution tier for `SEEDREAM_5_PRO`: `1K` or `2K` (default). The aspect ratio always follows `ref_asset`.

image_asset.description: Asset ID of the face-swapped image.

metadata.description:
Swap a face on a photo: the face from `face_asset` is placed onto the person in `ref_asset`, keeping the reference image's body, pose and scene. Image only — there is no video face swap. Output: one image with the face replaced.

**Models:**
- `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` *(default)* — Highest-quality swap. `swap_type` picks what is replaced: `face` (face only, reference's hairstyle kept), `head` (whole head including hair) or `person` (the person in `face_asset` replaces the person in `ref_asset`: face, hair and skin tone come from `face_asset`, while pose, body, outfit, background and light stay from the reference). `tier` picks 1K/2K; the output's aspect ratio always follows `ref_asset`.
- `FULL_HEAD` — Replaces the entire head, not just the face — use it when the target's hairstyle or head shape differs strongly from the source.

negative_prompt.description: Text describing what to avoid in the image.

batch_size.description: Must be 1: this tool generates one image per input. For N images pass N input objects.

model.description: Generation model, covering the WAN (incl. WAN 2.7 image), Nano Banana, Seedream, Qwen and Flux Klein families; `*_PRO` variants trade speed for higher quality. The general NSFW family is offered where the brand allows adult content.

ratio.description: Aspect ratio: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 2:3, 3:2 or 21:9 (default 1:1, square). `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` additionally supports 1:2, 2:1, 1:3, 3:1, 4:5, 5:4 and 9:21. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` also takes the four extreme banner ratios, up to eight to one. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` takes the 8 standard ratios only.

tier.description: Output resolution tier: `1K`, `2K` (default) or `4K`. `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` / `KREA_2` take `1K` or `2K`; models without a tier ignore it. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` also takes the top tier. `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` also take the top tier, in beta. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` takes `1K` or `2K`, at the same price. Other models reject `4K`.

thinking_level.description: Default `minimal` (fast); ignored by other models. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` also takes the longer-reasoning level for a more accurate result, +1 credit.

web_search.description: Default `false`; ignored by other models. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` can check Google Search for current facts, places and logos at the same price.

quality.description: Default `medium`, the level every model takes. `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` also take a cheaper draft level and a top level that adds detail, latency and credits. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` takes `low` / `medium` / `high` too.

transparent_background.description: Default `false`. `true` works on `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` only: they return a PNG with a transparent background (stickers, logos, product cut-outs) at the same price.

mode.description: Generation mode: `fast` (quicker and cheaper) or `quality` (slower, higher fidelity).

width.description: Optional output width in pixels; if omitted a size is derived from `ratio`.

height.description: Optional output height in pixels; if omitted a size is derived from `ratio`.

rewrite_prompt.description: For `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` / `IDEOGRAM_4_5` only: let the provider rewrite/expand the prompt before generation (default `false`). Leave off for NSFW prompts — the rewriter can corrupt them and produce an image unrelated to what was asked. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` may uppercase quoted text when it rewrites.

image_asset.description: Asset ID of the generated image.

metadata.description:
Generate an image from a text prompt, with no input image (text-to-image). The entry point for creation: use it when there is no source image and the picture is described in words — building a character or content from scratch, concepts, backgrounds, NSFW from a description, quick drafts and final hero shots. Supports fast/quality modes and aspect ratios; for several images pass several input objects, one per image.

**Three content groups (pick by what you need):**
- **Top cloud models, censored** (`GENERAL_NSFW`, `NANO_BANANA`, `NANO_BANANA_2_1`, `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE`, `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST`, `IDEOGRAM_4_5`) — highest quality and realism, but they block full NSFW content.
- **Uncensored, not built for full NSFW** (`WAN_2_7_IMAGE`, `QWEN_IMAGE`, `SEEDREAM_5`, `SEEDREAM_5_PRO`) — high quality and won't block, but won't create full NSFW content from scratch; they accurately **transform NSFW references** you provide.
- **Built for full NSFW** (`FLUX_KLEIN_NSFW`, `Z_IMAGE_SPICY`) — slightly lower quality and more artifacts, but real full-NSFW capability.

**Models:**
- `GENERAL_NSFW` *(default, trusted)* — General-purpose workhorse with a good quality/speed/price balance and strong facial likeness; the NSFW version is uncensored but does not produce full NSFW anatomy from text alone (it covers it up). Older model — occasional hand/limb artifacts.
- `GENERAL_SFW` — The same pipeline, SFW only.
- `WAN_2_7_IMAGE` / `WAN_2_7_IMAGE_PRO` — Modern model with higher quality and detail (Pro = top consistency). Renders bodies, scenes and composition more aesthetically and has fewer hand/limb artifacts. Weaker at in-image text. Uncensored, but transforms your NSFW references rather than inventing full NSFW content.
- `WAN` — Legacy WAN image model; prefer `WAN_2_7_IMAGE`.
- `Z_IMAGE_SPICY` *(trusted only)* — Z-Image Spicy (MuleRouter): uncensored photoreal images from text. `mode` picks `fast` (Standard, 1 credit) or `quality` (Pro, 2 credits); `ratio` is the only size control — `width`/`height`, `negative_prompt` and `tier` are ignored.
- `QWEN_IMAGE` / `QWEN_IMAGE_PRO` — Aesthetic results with good facial likeness and few artifacts; great for stylized / illustrative / anime subjects. Pro adds realism. Uncensored; transforms NSFW references.
- `SEEDREAM_5` — Newer generation: better prompt understanding, stronger stylization, better likeness, fewer artifacts. Uncensored; transforms NSFW references.
- `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` — The newest Seedream flagship: top prompt understanding and realism; supports all 15 aspect ratios and a `tier` resolution switch (`1K` = 2 credits, `2K` = 3 credits). Uncensored; transforms NSFW references.
- `NANO_BANANA` — Among the best for realism, and reliably renders legible in-image text (posters, signage, captions); strong real-world knowledge. Heavily censored — won't produce even mildly suggestive content. Weaker facial likeness.
- `NANO_BANANA_2_1` — Google Nano Banana 2.1: precise prompt following, consistent characters and legible in-image text (posters, infographics), up to 4K. Censored. The only model with the extra aspect ratios 4:1, 1:4, 8:1 and 1:8, `thinking_level` and `web_search`. Credits for `tier` 1K / 2K / 4K: 1 / 2 / 4, with `thinking_level` `high` 2 / 3 / 5.
- `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` — OpenAI GPT Image 2.5: strict prompt following, exact in-image copy and controlled layouts, up to 4K (`4K` is beta). Flare is faster, Sunburst is slower and more precise; same price. Censored. The 8 standard aspect ratios, `quality` and `transparent_background`. Credits for `tier` 1K / 2K / 4K: `quality` `low` 1 / 1 / 1, `medium` 1 / 1 / 2, `high` 2 / 3 / 5.
- `IDEOGRAM_4_5` — Ideogram 4.5: the best lettering of our models — readable quoted text, typography and logos on posters and signs. Censored. The 8 standard aspect ratios, `tier` 1K or 2K, `quality` and `rewrite_prompt`; no `negative_prompt`. Credits for `quality` `low` / `medium` / `high`: 1 / 2 / 6 at any `tier`.
- `FLUX_KLEIN_NSFW` *(trusted)* — The most advanced local full-NSFW model: creates uncensored NSFW content and also works with references — bring a character's face and create an action. Slightly lower quality, occasional artifacts.
- `KREA_2` *(trusted only)* — Krea v2 (WaveSpeed) with its built-in style LoRA; `negative_prompt`, `mode` and `width`/`height` are ignored. `tier` picks 1K (1 credit) / 2K (2 credits); `ratio` is the only size control.

Models marked *(trusted)* unlock NSFW behaviour only for trusted accounts (or accounts with an NSFW content policy).

ref_asset.description: Asset ID of the reference image to guide the generation.

face_asset.description: Asset ID of a face. `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` accepts it as a legacy alias and appends it to `character_assets`.

batch_size.description: Number of images to generate, 1-10. Default 4.

strength.description: How strongly the reference image constrains the result, 0.0-1.0 (higher sticks closer to the reference).

keep_pose.description: `SEEDREAM_5_PRO`: edit the reference in place, keeping its pose, body, outfit, lighting and background and swapping in the character's identity (face, hair, skin tone); the output keeps the reference's aspect. Default false.

body_asset.description: Legacy alias accepted only by `SEEDREAM_5_PRO`, appended to `character_assets` after `face_asset`. Rejected by the other models rather than ignored.

character_assets.description: Asset ID(s) of the character photo(s), 1-4. Required by `SEEDREAM_5_PRO`; the legacy `face_asset` and `body_asset` fields are folded into this list when sent.

ratio.description: Output aspect ratio for `SEEDREAM_5_PRO`: 1:1, 1:2, 2:1, 1:3, 3:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 16:9, 9:21 or 21:9. Defaults to the reference's own aspect; ignored with `keep_pose` and `CHARACTER_SWAP`.

image_assets.description: Asset IDs of the generated images (one per `batch_size`).

metadata.description: Recreate a reference photo's scene for your character (image-to-image). `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` recreates the reference's scene (pose, outfit, composition, light) for the character(s) from `character_assets` (required for this model, 1-4). With `keep_pose` the reference is instead edited in place: its pose, body, composition, outfit, lighting and background stay exactly as they are and only the person's identity (face, hair, skin tone) is taken from `character_assets`. Output size follows the reference by default, or a fixed `ratio` (ignored with `keep_pose`); `tier` picks 1K/2K. The pre-August `face_asset` and `body_asset` fields are still accepted and fold into `character_assets`.

face_ref.description: Asset ID of the face reference (upload via POST /assets).

body_ref.description: Asset ID of the body/pose reference (upload via POST /assets).

prompt.description: Free-text description of the shot (scene, outfit, lighting). Provide `prompt` for a custom shot, or `category_id` to use a curated category instead. If both are given, `category_id` takes precedence.

category_id.description: ID of a curated photoshoot category (see GET /photoshoot-categories). When set, the shot's prompts are taken from the category and `image_count` images are produced; it takes precedence over `prompt`.

image_count.description: Total number of images to generate (min 1). Drives how many shots are produced from the chosen `category_id` (or how many times `prompt` is repeated).

ratio.description: Aspect ratio of the output image: 1:1, 1:2, 2:1, 1:3, 3:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 16:9, 9:21 or 21:9 (default 1:1, square). Takes precedence over `width`/`height` when they describe a different shape.

width.description: Output width in pixels (default 1024; clamped to 512-4096).

height.description: Output height in pixels (default 1024; clamped to 512-4096).

number_of_images.description: Parallel images per shot (default 1); leave at 1 — use `image_count` to control the total.

rewrite_prompt.description: Let the provider rewrite/expand `prompt` before generation (default `false`). Leave off for NSFW prompts — the rewriter can corrupt them and produce an image unrelated to what was asked.

metadata.description: Run a consistent photoshoot of one character from a photo of the face and a photo of the body (without a face): each shot is generated from scratch, so poses come out organically different between frames — unlike `image_editor`, which keeps the source composition. The tool feeds the references through prepared prompt presets and returns a batch of images. Presets are grouped by category, so you can produce a set in a given style or action. Strength: reproducible, satisfying results with no manual prompting — at the cost of fine-grained control.

tier.description: Output resolution tier: `1K` (~1 MP) or `2K` (~4 MP). Default `2K`.

image_assets.description: Asset IDs of the generated face image(s).

metadata.description: Generate a brand-new face from structured attributes: gender, age, ethnicity, body type, eye/hair/beard colour, hairstyle, beard and makeup. No reference image; returns a single square image per request. Strength: full parametric control over the appearance — use it to create a fresh persona to reuse in other tools. For each attribute the accepted values are listed in that field's enum. Niche — used occasionally.

asset_ref.description: Asset ID of the subject/reference image.

tier.description: Output resolution tier: `1K` (~1 MP) or `2K` (~4 MP). Default `2K`.

width.description: Ignored: the output size is derived from `ratio` and `tier`.

height.description: Ignored: the output size is derived from `ratio` and `tier`.

number_of_images.description: Number of angle variations to generate, 1-10. Default 4.

image_assets.description: Asset IDs of the generated images (one per angle).

metadata.description: Bring an image and get the same subject from different camera angles (up to 10). Use it for social-media carousels and a "3D"/product overview of an object or character. Niche — used occasionally.

ref_asset.description: Asset ID of the starting image to animate (image-to-video). Required for all models except Seedance 2.0 and `seedance_2_5` in multimodal mode, where the images come from `ref_images` and `ref_asset` is optional (on `seedance_2_5` reference audio alone is enough), and `minimax@3.0*`, which also runs from a `last_frame` alone.

model.description: Video model. Kling: `kling@1.6`, `kling@2.1` (supports last_frame), `kling@2.5`, `kling@2.6`. WAN: `wan@2.2` (image-to-video, no last_frame), `wan@2.2-lora` (same as wan@2.2 but accepts `loras`), `wan@2.5`, `wan@2.6`, `wan@2.6-flash` (faster), `wan@2.7`, `wan@2.7-nsfw`, `wan@3.0`, `wan@3.0-nsfw`, `wan@3.0-prime` and `wan@3.0-prime-nsfw` (these support last_frame and a reference mode; the `-prime` pair runs the same model on a faster, slightly dearer queue). Seedance: `seedance_pro_fast`, `seedance_pro` (supports last_frame), `seedance_v1_5_pro` (supports last_frame), `seedance_2_0`, `seedance_2_0_fast`, `seedance_2_0_mini` (support last_frame and a multimodal reference mode), `seedance_2_5` *(trusted)* (the same, with wider limits, 1080p, up to 30 s and a `task_type`). Grok: `grok@4.1`. MiniMax: `minimax@3.0` (supports last_frame and a reference mode), `minimax@3.0-turbo` (supports last_frame). Default `wan@2.2`.

last_frame.description: Asset ID of the target final frame: the video interpolates from `ref_asset` to this frame. Only honoured by models that support it (`kling@2.1`, `seedance_pro`, `seedance_v1_5_pro`, `seedance_2_0`, `seedance_2_0_fast`, `seedance_2_0_mini`, `seedance_2_5`, `wan@3.0*`, `minimax@3.0*`); the older WAN models (incl. wan@2.2 and wan@2.7) do not support a last frame. `minimax@3.0*` also takes it without `ref_asset`, for an end-frame-only run.

audio_asset.description: Asset ID of an audio track to drive the video, for models that support audio input.

prompt.description: Text describing the desired motion and scene. Seedance 2.0, `seedance_2_5`, `wan@3.0*` and `minimax@3.0*` address the media as `[Image N]`, `[Video N]`, `[Audio N]`; the short `[img1]`, `[vid1]`, `[audio1]` the app inserts are accepted too and mean `[Image 1]`, `[Video 1]`, `[Audio 1]`.

duration.description: Clip length in seconds; valid values are model-dependent: `kling@2.6` → 5 or 10; `wan@2.2`, `wan@2.2-lora` → 5 or 8; `wan@2.6`, `wan@2.7`, `wan@2.7-lora`, `wan@2.7-nsfw` → 5, 10 or 15; `grok@4.1` → 6 or 10; `seedance_2_5` → 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30; `wan@3.0`, `wan@3.0-nsfw`, `wan@3.0-prime`, `wan@3.0-prime-nsfw` → 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25 or 30; everything else → 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 or 15. `-1` is not a length: it is `seedance_2_5` with a `task_type` of `edit`, where the result is exactly as long as the source, and no other model or task type accepts it. Any listed value is also accepted under `edit` and ignored. Default 5.

negative_prompt.description: Text describing what to avoid in the video.

resolution.description: Output resolution. Most models accept `720p` and `1080p`. `480p` is NOT supported by `wan@2.6`, `wan@2.6-flash`, `wan@2.7`, `wan@2.7-nsfw` or `seedance_v1_5_pro` (use 720p or 1080p for those). `wan@2.2`, `grok@4.1`, `seedance_2_0`, `seedance_2_0_fast` and `seedance_2_0_mini` accept only `480p` or `720p`. `wan@3.0*`, `minimax@3.0*` and `seedance_2_5` accept all three. Default `720p`, except `wan@3.0*`, which defaults to `480p`.

ratio.description: Aspect ratio: `adaptive`, `16:9`, `4:3`, `1:1`, `3:4`, `9:16`, `21:9`. Only the Seedance 2.0 models, `seedance_2_5`, `wan@3.0*` and `minimax@3.0` in its reference mode honour this, and `wan@3.0*` rejects `21:9`. On `seedance_2_5` it is ignored and forced to `adaptive` whenever the run has a first frame, or a `task_type` of `edit` or `extend`. Default `adaptive`.

seed.description: Seed for reproducibility (Seedance 2.0 models, `seedance_2_5`, `wan@3.0*` and `minimax@3.0*`). Default random.

generate_audio.description: Generate an audio track too, for models that support it. `minimax@3.0*` always returns one and cannot be silenced — the switch does not reach it. Default true.

camera_fixed.description: Keep the camera fixed instead of letting it move. Default false.

prompt_extend.description: Let the model auto-expand and enhance your prompt. On `minimax@3.0*` it picks the slower, richer rewrite (~30 s) over the one-second default. Default false.

loras.description: LoRA styles to apply, as a map of LoRA id to a scale-settings object (`{high_scale?, low_scale?}`, both optional — not a bare number). Only `wan@2.2-lora` uses this; browse compatible ids via GET /loras?model=wan@2.2.

ref_images.description: Seedance 2.0, `seedance_2_5`, `wan@3.0*` and `minimax@3.0` reference mode: extra reference image asset IDs (up to 8 in addition to `ref_asset`; `seedance_2_5` takes 30 images counting `ref_asset`). Reference them in the prompt as `[Image N]`.

ref_videos.description: Seedance 2.0 and `minimax@3.0` multimodal mode: reference video asset IDs (up to 3, ≤15 s total; `seedance_2_5` takes up to 10, ≤30 s total and 2-30 s each). Reference them in the prompt as `[Video N]`. This is the video-to-video path. `wan@3.0*` takes video references only in the video2video tool.

ref_audios.description: Seedance 2.0, `seedance_2_5`, `wan@3.0*` and `minimax@3.0` reference mode: reference audio asset IDs (up to 3, ≤15 s in total across all of them; `seedance_2_5` takes up to 10, ≤30 s in total, and accepts audio with no image or video beside it). A longer total is refused before the run, with no charge. Reference them in the prompt as `[Audio N]` (`minimax@3.0` also needs a reference image or video alongside).

task_type.description: `seedance_2_5` with references only: what the model does with the reference videos. `auto` (default) lets the model decide from the wording of the prompt — which can silently turn the run into an edit and refuse the requested length. `reference` drives a NEW clip from the references. `edit` changes one reference video in place (exactly one video; the result is as long as the source and is billed for twice its length). `extend` continues one reference video by `duration` more seconds. `edit` and `extend` force `ratio` to `adaptive`, and `edit` takes `duration` as `-1` and ignores any other value. Omit it for frame runs and for every other model.

video_asset.description: Asset ID of the generated video.

metadata.description:
Animate a photo into a video (image-to-video). Cost depends on the model, duration (5-15 s, up to 30 s on the `wan@3.0` line) and resolution (480p-1080p). Supports prompt enhancement, fixed camera, LoRAs and optional audio. Quick guide: general content (best price/quality) — Seedance; NSFW content — `wan@2.7-nsfw` or `wan@2.2-lora`; tasteful content with complex actions — Kling (censored).

**Wan** — the `wan@2.7` and `wan@3.0` lines understand prompts best and animate a first frame well (1080p, good physics, up to 5 references):
- `wan@3.0` — Newest Wan; native audio, first frame (+ optional last frame) or references, 480p/720p/1080p and clips up to 30 s. No `21:9`. A run takes 15-55 minutes (hours at 1080p x 30 s), so poll instead of waiting on it.
- `wan@3.0-nsfw` *(trusted)* — The same model with content inspection lifted; identical fields, price and timings.
- `wan@3.0-prime` — The same model on a faster queue: identical fields and results, about 40% quicker, roughly 10% dearer. Pick it when the wait matters more than the price.
- `wan@3.0-prime-nsfw` *(trusted)* — The prime queue with content inspection lifted.
- `wan@2.7` — Previous line; top prompt understanding and first-frame animation, and much faster than the `wan@3.0` line.
- `wan@2.7-nsfw` *(trusted)* — Wan 2.7 for NSFW; the best choice when you have a first frame (or a frame with an action) to animate.
- `wan@2.6` / `wan@2.6-flash` — Cheaper and older; **flash** is even cheaper and faster.
- `wan@2.5` — Older generation; prefer `wan@2.6` or `wan@2.7`.
- `wan@2.2` — Animates a first frame; uncensored NSFW base.
- `wan@2.2-lora` — Presets with action-trained LoRAs that turn a first frame into a complex action. Includes "Blink" LoRAs: bring any photo of your character and the frame morphs into the desired NSFW action. The **easiest option for beginners** — no prompt needed, just a photo similar to the example's first frame.

**Kling** — censored, but animates a first frame well; newer versions cost more and understand prompts and complex actions better:
- `kling@2.6` — Top motion and physics, plus native audio (dialogue, effects).
- `kling@2.5` — High quality, cheaper, consistent at volume.
- `kling@2.1` — Stable motion.
- `kling@1.6` — Oldest and cheapest Kling.

**Seedance** — uncensored; best price/quality balance for content:
- `seedance_pro_fast` — Faster and cheaper, less "smart".
- `seedance_pro` — Pricier and smarter.
- `seedance_v1_5_pro` — Best quality and result; joint audio+video, micro-expressions, first+last frame.
- `seedance_2_0` — Latest line; first/first+last frame, native audio, fixed camera, and a multimodal mode (pass `ref_images`/`ref_videos`/`ref_audios` to drive generation by references addressed in the prompt as `[Image N]`/`[Video N]`/`[Audio N]`). 480p/720p only.
- `seedance_2_0_fast` — Faster and cheaper Seedance 2.0; no fixed camera.
- `seedance_2_0_mini` — Cheapest Seedance 2.0 variant.
- `seedance_2_5` *(trusted)* — Same shape as Seedance 2.0 with wider limits: up to 30 s, 1080p, 30 images + 10 videos + 10 audios of references (≤30 s of video in total), and a `task_type` that says whether the references drive a new clip, an edit of one of them, or its continuation.

**Grok:**
- `grok@4.1` — Censored; animates a first frame, top image-to-video, always with native audio.

**MiniMax** — censored, native audio, 480p/720p/1080p and 5-15 s. Trusted accounts have the provider-side filter lifted; the model still refuses explicit briefs itself, and a refused run is failed and refunded rather than billed:

image_assets.description: Asset ID(s) of the source image(s). Pass a single id to edit one image, or several (as an array) to combine them into one result (unless `batch_mode` is set). When `ratio` is not set, the combined result inherits the first image's geometry — put the scene or base image first and face/detail references after it (in `batch_mode` each image keeps its own geometry).

prompt.description: Instruction describing the edit to apply.

model.description: Editing model. `GENERAL_NSFW` — general-purpose editor (default, allows NSFW); `SEEDREAM_4_5` — the same general-purpose editor under another name; `NANO_BANANA` — Google Nano Banana; `QWEN_IMAGE` / `QWEN_IMAGE_PRO` — Qwen editors (Pro = higher quality); `SEEDREAM_5` — Seedream; `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` — the newest Seedream flagship (up to 10 references); `FLUX_KLEIN_NSFW` — Flux Klein editor; `FLUX_KLEIN_LORA` — Flux Klein with a style template (requires `loras` or `lora_id`); `WAN_2_7_IMAGE` / `WAN_2_7_IMAGE_PRO` — WAN 2.7 editors (Pro = higher quality); `NANO_BANANA_2_1` — Google Nano Banana 2.1 (up to 14 references and the top tier); `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` — OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (up to 16 references and the top tier, Sunburst is more precise in edits); `IDEOGRAM_4_5` — Ideogram 4.5 (best lettering, up to 5 images).

ratio.description: Aspect ratio (e.g. 1:1, 16:9, 9:16). Overrides width/height when set. When omitted the ratio of the first source image is used and the result is centre-cropped to it, so set `ratio` explicitly whenever the output needs a specific framing. `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` supports 15 ratios (adds 1:2, 2:1, 1:3, 3:1, 4:5, 5:4 and 9:21). `NANO_BANANA_2_1` also takes the four extreme banner ratios and, when the ratio is omitted, follows the first image uncropped. `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` take the 8 standard ratios and, when it is omitted, use the standard ratio closest to the first image, uncropped. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` ignores it: the result keeps the first image's size.

tier.description: Output resolution tier: `1K`, `2K` (default) or `4K`. `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` takes `1K` or `2K`; models without a tier ignore it. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` also takes the top tier. `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` also take the top tier, in beta. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` takes `1K` or `2K`, at the same price. Other models reject `4K`.

thinking_level.description: Default `minimal` (fast); ignored by other models. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` also takes the longer-reasoning level for a more accurate result, +1 credit.

web_search.description: Default `false`; ignored by other models. `NANO_BANANA_2_1` can check Google Search for current facts, places and logos at the same price.

quality.description: Default `medium`, the level every model takes. `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` also take a cheaper draft level and a top level that adds detail, latency and credits. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` takes `low` / `medium` / `high` too.

transparent_background.description: Default `false`. `true` works on `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` only: they return a PNG with a transparent background (stickers, logos, product cut-outs) at the same price.

width.description: Output width in pixels (default 1024). Used when `ratio` is not set.

height.description: Output height in pixels (default 1024). Used when `ratio` is not set.

batch_mode.description: When several `image_assets` are given, edit each one separately (one result per image) instead of combining them into a single image. Default false.

sequential_generation.description: Generate the requested images one after another, each conditioned on the previous result (for consistent, story-like sequences) instead of independently. Default false.

lora_id.description: Deprecated: use `loras` instead. ID of a LoRA style template to apply (when `model=FLUX_KLEIN_LORA`). Browse available templates and their ids via GET /templates.

loras.description: LoRA style templates to apply when `model=FLUX_KLEIN_LORA`, as a map of LoRA id to a scale-settings object (`{high_scale?, low_scale?}`, both optional — not a bare number). Browse ids via GET /templates. All LoRAs must share the same model.

rewrite_prompt.description: For `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` only: let the provider rewrite/expand the prompt before generation (default `false`). Leave off for NSFW prompts — the rewriter can corrupt them and produce an image unrelated to what was asked.

mask_asset.description: For `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` / `IDEOGRAM_4_5` only: asset ID of a PNG mask the size of the first image. On a mask with transparency every painted pixel, any colour, marks the area to edit and transparent pixels are kept; on an opaque mask white marks the area and black keeps it. The mask does not change the price, takes one image slot and is not allowed with `batch_mode`. `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` read it as guidance: the change lands in the area, the border is approximate and pixels outside may shift slightly; at most 15 `image_assets`. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` edits only the area and needs part of the image left unpainted; at most 4 `image_assets`.

edit_precision.description: Default `regular`. `IDEOGRAM_4_5` takes `high` for a precise edit: it changes only what the prompt asks and restores every other pixel, at the same price.

image_assets.description: Asset IDs of the edited images.

metadata.description:
Edit and composite existing images by prompt — the main, most flexible image tool. Bring references, edit and combine them; bring your character and dress them from a reference photo; keep a product or object **exactly** (fabric, pattern, shape) while changing the scene. It offers both SFW and NSFW models, plus LoRA presets that extend NSFW capability. You are limited mainly by your imagination. Edits inherit the source composition (pose, framing), so for a photoshoot-style series of varied organic poses of one character use `photoshoot` instead.

**Models:**
- `GENERAL_NSFW` *(default, trusted)* — Universal default, uncensored, good facial likeness; general NSFW edits such as outfit or pose changes. Older model — occasional limb artifacts.
- `NANO_BANANA` — High realism and the most precise prompt-driven edits; good at edits involving in-image text. Heavily censored (no NSFW); weaker likeness.
- `NANO_BANANA_2_1` — Google Nano Banana 2.1: precise edits and composites from up to 14 references (the first is the base image), consistent characters and legible in-image text, up to 4K. Censored. The only editor with the extra aspect ratios 4:1, 1:4, 8:1 and 1:8, `thinking_level` and `web_search`; the result keeps the provider's size. Credits per image for `tier` 1K / 2K / 4K: 2 / 2 / 4, with `thinking_level` `high` 2 / 3 / 5, independent of the number of references.
- `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_FLARE` / `GPT_IMAGE_2_5_SUNBURST` — OpenAI GPT Image 2.5: controlled edits that keep the person, product and layout, exact in-image copy, up to 16 references (the first is the base image), up to 4K (`4K` is beta). Flare is faster, Sunburst is slower and more precise in edits; same price. Censored. `quality`, `transparent_background` and `mask_asset`; without `ratio` the result takes the standard ratio closest to the first image, uncropped. Credits per image for `tier` 1K / 2K / 4K with up to 4 references: `quality` `low` 2 / 2 / 2, `medium` 2 / 3 / 3, `high` 3 / 5 / 6; each started 3 references above 4 add 1 credit (5-7: +1, 8-10: +2, 11-13: +3, 14-16: +4).
- `IDEOGRAM_4_5` — Ideogram 4.5: precise edits that leave untouched areas as they were, the best at fixing text and logos, up to 5 images (the first is edited, the rest only guide). Censored. `quality`, `edit_precision` and `mask_asset`; the result keeps the first image's size, so `ratio` and `tier` are ignored. Credits per image for `quality` `low` / `medium` / `high`: 1 / 2 / 6.
- `QWEN_IMAGE` / `QWEN_IMAGE_PRO` — Aesthetic, good likeness, few artifacts; Pro adds realism. Uncensored; transforms your NSFW references rather than creating full NSFW content from scratch.
- `SEEDREAM_5` — Newer than the default: better prompt understanding, stronger stylization, better likeness, fewer artifacts. Uncensored; transforms NSFW references.
- `SEEDREAM_5_PRO` — The newest Seedream flagship editor: up to 10 reference images (their order is preserved), all 15 aspect ratios and a `tier` resolution switch (`1K` = 2 credits, `2K` = 3 credits, independent of the number of references). Uncensored; transforms NSFW references.
- `WAN_2_7_IMAGE` / `WAN_2_7_IMAGE_PRO` — Aesthetic bodies and composition, few artifacts, precise editing; Pro = higher quality. Uncensored; transforms NSFW references. Weaker at in-image text.
- `FLUX_KLEIN_NSFW` *(trusted)* — Local flagship for full NSFW with references: it knows anatomy and accepts a face reference. Slightly lower quality, occasional artifacts.
- `FLUX_KLEIN_LORA` *(trusted)* — LoRA presets that extend NSFW capability (including clothing-removal presets) and style templates; pass `loras` or `lora_id` (browse via GET /templates).

Models marked *(trusted)* unlock NSFW behaviour only for trusted accounts (or accounts with an NSFW content policy).

- `wan@2.7` *(default)* — Top quality, 720p/1080p, up to 15 s.
- `wan@2.2` — Budget option.
- `wan@3.0` / `wan@3.0-nsfw` *(the nsfw entry: trusted, not in every region)* — Direct text-to-video with native audio; 480p/720p/1080p, durations 5/6/8/10/12/15/20/25/30 s, prompts up to 20000 characters. No `21:9`. Generation takes 15-55 minutes (hours at 1080p/30 s).
- `wan@3.0-prime` / `wan@3.0-prime-nsfw` — The same pair on a faster queue: identical fields and results, about 40% quicker, roughly 10% dearer.
- `seedance_2_0` / `seedance_2_0_fast` / `seedance_2_0_mini` — Direct text-to-video (no first-frame step); native audio, fixed camera (non-fast), durations 5/6/8/10/12/15 s. All three are 480p/720p only; `seedance_2_0_mini` is the cheapest of the three.
- `seedance_2_5` *(trusted)* — The same, reaching further: 480p/720p/1080p and durations 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30 s.
- `minimax@3.0` / `minimax@3.0-turbo` — Censored; direct text-to-video with native audio, 480p/720p/1080p, durations 5/6/8/10/12/15 s. Turbo is faster and half the price.

resolution.description: Target output resolution: `1080p`, `2k` or `4k`. Higher costs more. Default `1080p`.

metadata.description: Bring a medium-quality video and get a sharper, higher-resolution result via BytePlus vCube. Pick a quality tier (`standard` — fast and affordable, or `pro` — premium model) and a target output resolution (`1080p`, `2k` or `4k`). Output is locked to 30fps. Priced per output second by tier x resolution x duration.
